findings: No S1 or S2 problems in data group 1 (analyseVectorCondition('if', bits)). The model follows IEEE 1800-2023 §12.4, which says the first statement runs when the condition 'has a nonzero known value' and does not run when the condition has a zero value or the value is x or z. The same clause gives 'if (expression)' and 'if (expression != 0)' as the same logic. Here, truth comes from truthOf: any 1 bit is true, all 0 bits is false, otherwise unknown. branch comes from ifBranch: only true runs then. notEqualZero is compare('!=', e, fromNumber(0, width)).result, so 4'b1x00 gives 1 (a known bit differs, §11.4.5), 4'b0x00 gives x and 4'b0000 gives 0. The why strings say 'if (e) tests e != 0' and 'an x or z result counts as false', which match the clause text. All 27 tests in tests/components/LogicStateDiagram.test.tsx pass (vitest run).

S3 src/components/visuals/LogicStateDiagram.tsx:618 - 4'b1x00 is treated as 'true' because it is known nonzero, although the value is not fully known. §12.4's phrase 'nonzero known value' does not settle this by itself; the reading rests on the clause's own if (e) == if (e != 0) equivalence plus §11.4.5 giving e != 0 = 1. It matches the LRM and common simulator behaviour, but it is an interpretation -> optionally have the why string say that the known 1 bit makes e != 0 a known 1, so e counts as a known nonzero value.

S3 tests/components/LogicStateDiagram.test.tsx:212-218 - the z cases (0z0z, 0z01) pin only .branch, and 0000 pins only the start of its why string. The z-specific notEqualZero values (x and 1), oneBits/unknownBits ([0]/[2], []/[2,0]), and the full why strings (including 'bits 2, 0 are x or z') are not pinned -> add toBe assertions on notEqualZero, the bit lists and the full why string for 0z0z, 0z01 and 0000.

Verified, no S1/S2 in group 2. IEEE 1800-2023 §11.4.7 says the unary logical negation operator (!) turns a nonzero or true operand into 1'b0 and a zero or false operand into 1'b1, and that an ambiguous truth value results in 1'bx. §12.4 says the first statement runs only when the condition has a nonzero known value, and a zero, x or z value counts as false. logicalNot (src/lib/sv-four-state-model.ts:217) and ifBranch (:349) follow these rules. In analyseVectorCondition (src/components/visuals/LogicStateDiagram.tsx:634-641): 0x00 gives !e = x and the else branch, 1x00 gives !e = 0 and else, 0000 gives !e = 1 and then. tests/components/LogicStateDiagram.test.tsx:220-230 pins all three branches, both negated values and the 1'bx explanation, and the test passes. The 1-bit IfPanel text '!x is still x (§11.4.7) ... both take else (§12.4)' (LogicStateDiagram.tsx:517-525) is consistent with these rules.

S3 tests/components/LogicStateDiagram.test.tsx:226-229 - the why strings for the ifnot cases 1x00 ('!e is 1'b0 (§11.4.7), so the else branch runs') and 0000 are not pinned; only negated and branch are -> add toMatch assertions on known.why and on the 0000 why.

S3 src/components/visuals/LogicStateDiagram.tsx:660 - for if (!e) with an unknown e, a 'then' guess gets 'An x or z bit might be 0, so e is not known to be nonzero.' That speaks about e, not !e, so it does not say why !e fails to be true. The r.why sentence that follows does explain it -> for construct 'ifnot', use a lead-in like 'e is not known to be zero, so !e is x, not 1.'

Verified against IEEE 1800-2023 §11.4.11 and Table 11-20 (t1_lrm_clean.txt, offset about 820807). A true condition returns the first expression and a false one returns the second. With an ambiguous (x or z) condition, both expressions are evaluated and compared with the §11.4.5 logical equality. If they are not equal, Table 11-20 merges them bit by bit. The table rows are 0: 0 x x x; 1: x 1 x x; x: all x; z: all x. CONDITIONAL_MERGE in sv-four-state-model.ts:407 ('0xxx','x1xx','xxxx','xxxx') matches the table, and conditionalOp (sv-four-state-model.ts:414-421) puts the logical-equality check before the merge. truthOf (line 208) treats any known 1 as true, all 0s as false and everything else as ambiguous, so 0x00 gives y=x, 1x00 gives y=1 and 0000 gives y=0. All three match the LRM. The 1-bit IfPanel (LogicStateDiagram.tsx:493-512) still uses conditionalOp([a],['1'],['0']) and its §11.4.11/Table 11-20 text is unchanged. No S1 or S2 found.

S3 tests/components/LogicStateDiagram.test.tsx:232-238 - the ternary model test checks y for 0x00 and 1x00 and checks why only against /Table 11-20/. It never checks the false case (0000 gives y=1'b0, 'returns the second value') or the full why strings for the true, false and ambiguous branches, although the builder's notes say tests check the full explanation strings -> add analyseVectorCondition('ternary', parseBits('0000')).y === '0' and toBe() checks on all three ternary why strings.

S3 src/components/visuals/LogicStateDiagram.tsx:630 - the ambiguous-condition text says ?: 'evaluates both 1'b1 and 1'b0 and merges them bit by bit'. It leaves out the §11.4.11 step that compares the two results for logical equivalence first and returns either one when they are equal. The result for 1 vs 0 is right, but a learner may conclude that ?: always merges -> add 'they differ (1'b1 != 1'b0), so ...' before the merge clause.

S3 src/components/visuals/LogicStateDiagram.tsx:735-739 - the ternary reveal also shows the note 'if (e) is the same test as if (e != 0) (§12.4)', which is about if statements, not ?:. It is true but off-topic for the ?: construct -> show that note only when construct !== 'ternary', or change it to name the ?: condition's truth for ternary.

Verified, no S1/S2 in group 4. IEEE 1800-2023 §12.5 says a plain case match succeeds only when 'each bit matches exactly with respect to the values 0, 1, x, and z', and items are compared in order with the first match winning. §12.5.1 says z is a do-not-care for casez, x and z are do-not-cares for casex, in 'either the case_expression or the case_items', and ? may stand for z. caseItemMatches and selectCaseItem in src/lib/sv-four-state-model.ts:360-375 implement exactly this. I ran the model over sel in {x0,1z,z1,11,x1,0x} for all three kinds against A 2'b00, B 2'b1?, C 2'bx1. Results: case x0 -> default D, casez x0 -> D, casex x0 -> A, casez 1z -> B, casex 0x -> A. Every one matches the LRM.

Verified: CASE_ITEMS (LogicStateDiagram.tsx:441-445) are A 2'b00, B 2'b1?, C 2'bx1 plus default D, in the same order and with the same labels as the lesson prose (flow-control.mdx:116 in this worktree). initialValue for the case panel accepts only width 2 (line 460), and x01 falls back to x0. The text also says 'the unknown bit' (singular) when two bits are ignored, as in casez z1 vs B 'ignores bits 1, 0'. -> Say 'including the z bit of the case expression' for casez and 'the x/z bit' for casex, and make the noun agree with the number of bits.

S1 src/components/visuals/LogicStateDiagram.tsx:660 - The prefix 'An x or z bit might be 0, so e is not known to be nonzero.' is used for every wrong 'then' guess when truth is 'unknown', including if (!e). For if (!4'b0x00) that is the wrong correction. A learner who picks 'then' has assumed e is 0, so !e is 1. Telling them e is not known to be nonzero supports their guess instead of refuting it. The real reason is in §11.4.7: !e gives 1'bx when the operand's truth is ambiguous, and §12.4 says an x condition is false, so the else branch runs. -> Limit this prefix to r.construct === 'if'. S3 tests/components/LogicStateDiagram.test.tsx:240 - The diagnostics test checks only the 'if' construct (1x00 else/x, 0x00 then), and two checks are prefix-only regexes. Verified correct, no action needed: 'An if statement cannot produce x by itself: it runs one branch' (line 659) matches §12.4. A cond_predicate that evaluates to x or z is false, so if/else runs exactly one statement and y is a clean 0 or 1. The prefix appears only for ternary with truth 'unknown' and a wrong guess of 1 or 0. 'One known 1 is enough' appears only for 'if' with truth 'true', unknown bits present and guess 'else', which is the only case where it is true (§12.4: 'if (expression)' is the same test as 'if (expression != 0)'). build:expression-tree-explorer.notes:
Design
- The model (src/lib/sv-expression-tree-presets.ts) never evaluates an operator. Values, widths, roles and steps come from sv-expression-model, imported only:
  - parseExpression and annotateTree;
  - evaluateAssignment, for the step-through and stored values;
  - mathIntuition, for the exact sum in the carry text;
  - splitConcatTarget, for `{carry, s8}`.
- What the model adds:
  - PRECEDENCE_ROWS: the supported rows of Table 11-2, used only to explain why the parser grouped as it did. A test checks every pair of binary operators against parseExpression, so the row table cannot drift from the parser.
  - Grouping options (the parser's tree, rotations of the root, and the author's version when it uses the same tokens), sorted by text so position gives nothing away.
  - Operator positions in the source, for the tap prediction.
  - Tree layout.
  - bowlsOf: the bowl split, from §11.6.1 Table 11-21 and §11.8.2.
  - Width presets, with every option and feedback text generated.
- Distractor stored values are computed by re-running the statement with `W'(a + b)` size casts for W = 8, 9 and 32. Their feedback says "what a bowl of W bits gives".

Judgement calls
- The intended version of each precedence preset is my reading of the likely intent, for example `(a || b) && c`, `2 ** (3 ** 2)` and `-(2 ** 2)`.
- For conditional-chain, the parser's grouping already is the intended one, so the panel says "No flip".
- chained-compare's fix is `(a < b) && (b < c)`, not a parenthesizat

Verified against the sources: §16.12.7 (IEEE 1800-2023) says an implication with no antecedent match 'succeeds and returns true'. §16.14.8 says a |-> b with a false is a vacuous success that 'is not considered a pass or a failure', which matches the focus text at src/lib/sva-model.ts:1984 and the status wording. §16.14.5 says a new evaluation attempt begins at every leading clock event, which matches the one attempt per edge (8 attempts for 8 edges). §16.7 ##N means gnt is checked only at edge s+N, which matches the met message at src/lib/sva-model.ts:2028.

S1 src/lib/sva-model.ts:1424 (and doc comment :1361) - the reason text a learner sees, 'every consequent was itself vacuously true (§16.14.8 h)', names the wrong list item. In IEEE 1800-2023 §16.14.8, item h) is if/else. Item i) is `sequence_expression |-> property_expr` and item j) is `|=>`. I mapped the letters in t1_lrm_clean.txt: a) sequence, b) strong, c) weak, d) not, e) or, f) and, g) if, h) if-else, i) |->, j) |=>. The a), e) and f) citations elsewhere are correct. -> Cite '§16.14.8 i' for |-> and '§16.14.8 j' for |=> (choose by node.overlapping), fix the comment the same way, and add a test that pins the letter.

S1 src/lib/sva-model.ts:1555-1560 - diagnoseAttempt says 'the antecedent did not match, so the consequent was never checked' (wrong prediction PASS) and 'Nothing was checked, because the antecedent did not match' (wrong prediction FAIL) for every VACUOUS result. That is false when the model returns VACUOUS for other reasons. I ran it: `c |-> (a |-> b)` with c=1, a=0 is VACUOUS with reason 'the antecedent matched, but every consequent was itself vacuously true', and `(a |-> b) and (a |-> c)` with a=0 is VACUOUS through §16.14.8 f). In both cases the diagnosis still says the antecedent did not match. A learner can reach both through the property editor. -> Build the message from attempt.reason, or branch on why the attempt is vacuous: antecedent did not match / the antecedent matched but the consequent was vacuous (§16.14.8 i/j) / both and-or operands vacuous (§16.14.8 e/f). Add tests for the nested and the `and` case.

S1 src/lib/sva-model.ts:1296-1303 - the `not` case drops vacuity, which contradicts §16.14.8 d): 'not property_expr is nonvacuous if, and only if, the underlying evaluation attempt of property_expr is nonvacuous'. I ran it: `not not (a |-> b)` with a=0 returns PASS, a real pass ('`not` holds because ... failed'). By d) applied twice, that attempt is vacuous, so it is a vacuous success, not a pass. The inner FAIL also loses the information that it was vacuous. -> Carry a `vacuous` flag through the not case. A vacuous operand that is true or false keeps vacuous, and a vacuous true result maps to VACUOUS, never PASS. Add a test for `not not (a |-> b)`.

S3 src/lib/sva-model.ts:1300-1302 - question, not confirmed: `not (a |-> b)` with a false is reported as a plain FAIL, citing §16.12.3. The value is right (false). It does not say how a vacuous false result is reported. -> Mention in the reason or the assumptions that this result is vacuous by §16.14.8 d), and that tools still run the fail action because the property is false.
